2
What we built

Point it at a window. Thirty seconds later, a diagnosis — and every dimension it checked, with the numbers.

3
Architecture

Everything is ClickHouse. Seven stages are SQL. One is the LLM.

Delete stage 6 and the diagnosis is unchanged. The LLM receives computed numbers, never an event row.

4
Schema · the negative result

We built the obvious rollup first, and measured it.

Fully crossed · hour × 9 dims

7,247,816

rows from 7.2M events.
Nearly every event its own combination.
It compressed nothing.

Unpivoted · (hour, dim_name, dim_value)

53,760

Only 62 distinct dimension values exist in total.
167× smaller — and exactly the shape contribution ranking reads.

SummingMergeTree, not Aggregating — every measure is additive, so -State/-Merge would buy nothing. Dictionaries, not JOINs — nine dimensions resolved by dictGet() at insert time. No statistic is materialized — the baseline window is a parameter; freezing it at write time returns the wrong answer.

6
The SQL

One ARRAY JOIN fans every event into one row per dimension

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW inmobi.mv_events_hourly_by_dim
TO inmobi.events_hourly_by_dim AS
SELECT toStartOfHour(event_time) AS hour, d.1 AS dim_name, d.2 AS dim_value,
       count() AS requests, sum(is_filled) AS fills,
       sum(is_impression) AS impressions, sum(revenue) AS revenue
FROM inmobi.ad_events
ARRAY JOIN [
  ('os_version',  dictGetString('inmobi.dict_geo_device','os_version', geo_device_id)),
  ('region',      dictGetString('inmobi.dict_geo_device','region',     geo_device_id)),
  ('category',    dictGetString('inmobi.dict_apps','category',         app_id)),
  ...9 dimensions
] AS d
GROUP BY hour, dim_name, dim_value;

The dictionaries resolve every dimension at insert time, so the view never JOINs. Ratios are never stored — fill rate, CTR and eCPM are recomputed as sum/sum on read, because averaging per-hour ratios is silently wrong the moment bucket sizes differ.

Same day. Four ways of looking.

What it ruled out · 2026-06-21

Saying “no segment is responsible” is the finding

DimensionVerdictBecause
publisher_tieruniformall 3 values within 0.2% of the global −4.4%
ad_formatuniformall 5 values within 0.4%
categoryuniformall 7 values within 0.5%
campaign_typenot applicablefill rate is 1.0 by construction — the field only exists once a request has filled

The bug this prevents. Ranking segments by size of drop named tier_1 responsible for a 315-request deviation out of an incident of 97,027 — 0.3%. Confident, reproducible, wrong.

10
The unseen incident · 2026-07-06 → 07-10 · run cold

1.5M fresh events. One command, 37 seconds.

A · Jul 6 — mix shift

Request share moved: APAC + LATAM +17pp, EU + NAM −13pp. The two cheapest regions displaced the two most expensive.

No region’s own eCPM changed. Global eCPM still fell ~8% — dilution, not a price change.

B · Jul 9 — real price change

video eCPM −30%, rewarded +26%, everything else flat.

Shares did not move. So this one is genuine, not a mix effect.

RunWhat our system saidVerdict
B Jul 9–10 ecpm in ad_format=video −35.0% vs −12.0% Correct — segment, magnitude, direction
A Jul 6–8 requests in campaign_type=CPC +139.5% vs +8.6% Right window & factor — named CPC; region=APAC ranked 5th of 7
Full 119h one event, ecpm in ad_format=video Partly — merged A and B into one

Why we missed A’s cause. Our attribution asks whether a segment’s metric moved beyond what its size explains. In a mix shift no segment’s metric moves — only the weights do. Catching it needs a share-of-volume decomposition alongside the metric one. We did not build that.

12
What's new — and what isn't

Three claims

  • It reports what it ruled out, with numbers. On a uniform drop the correct answer is “no segment is responsible” — and most systems will confidently name one anyway.
  • It finds compound segments that no single-dimension scan can see.
  • The LLM writes only the sentence. It receives computed numbers, never an event; every figure in its prose is matched back to the evidence, and the run exits non-zero if one cannot be.

And the honest limits

We see the shape of a change, not the system that caused it — we say what the evidence is consistent with and name what a human should check. Compound search is pairs, not triples. Thresholds are judgment calls anchored to measurements on one dataset, each listed in METHOD.md with how it fails; we have run no sensitivity sweep.

13
Does it work in real time?

Yes — and it needed no new maths

The materialized views are insert triggers: they fire on every INSERT regardless of source — Kafka, ClickPipes, an HTTP POST from an edge collector. No batch job, no cron, no recompute. And because no statistic is materialized, there is nothing to drift or rebuild. One pass over a 48-hour window is ~1.2 s; at a 60-second poll that is under 5% duty cycle.

The edge case batch testing cannot surface

Run at 14:30 and the newest hour holds thirty minutes of traffic. Against a full-hour baseline that reads as a ~50% collapse — on every run, forever.

The arithmetic is correct, the baseline is correct, the comparison is invalid — exactly the failure this project exists to prevent. It never appears in testing, because the provided dataset ends on a complete hour. It would appear within minutes of going live.

Fixed: an inferred window stops one hour short, because in an append-only stream an hour is only provably complete once a later hour exists. An explicit --end is still honoured — the caller stated the window and owns it.

Also handled: alert dedup across passes, so a 3-day incident pages once, not 72 times. Not built: incident state that survives restarts, backfill-aware baselines for late-arriving events, per-tenant isolation, alert routing. PRODUCTION.md lists each one.

14
At 100× · and where to find it

We measured which stage doesn't scale

StageRows readTimeReads
Compound scan1,211,930,49643.2 sraw events
Everything else — detect, decompose, localize, rule out6,104,5329.7 srollups

One stage is 99.5% of the rows. The rollup holds 53,760 rows at 9M events — and at 900M, because it grows with distinct values × hours, not events. The fix for the outlier is the trick we already used once: a pair rollup, ~33,600 rows.
